name: High Scores and Hidden Levels: The Games We All Played
description: From a spaceship duel on a college computer to Minecraft and Fortnite: the games, consoles and crashes that built a billion-dollar way to play.

checkpoints.name: Lab toys and arcades
checkpoints.note: Spacewar! is a duel for college computers, The Oregon Trail teaches schoolchildren history, the Magnavox Odyssey brings games to home television, Pong makes the arcade, and Colossal Cave Adventure is a game of words. The Atari 2600 puts cartridges in the living room.

checkpoints.name: The golden age of the arcade
checkpoints.note: Space Invaders, Asteroids, Pac-Man and Donkey Kong fill arcades with quarters. The Video game crash of 1983 hits hard, and then the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) brings the industry back.

checkpoints.name: Mario, Sonic and the PC
checkpoints.note: Super Mario Bros., Tetris, The Legend of Zelda and the Game Boy make Nintendo the king. Sega Genesis answers with Sonic the Hedgehog, the Super Nintendo and Street Fighter II battle on, Civilization, Doom and Myst bring ideas to the PC, and the PlayStation arrives in 1994.

checkpoints.name: The 3D revolution
checkpoints.note: Quake, Tomb Raider, Super Mario 64, Final Fantasy VII and Half-Life move games into three dimensions, StarCraft and World of Warcraft go online, and Grand Theft Auto III, The Sims, PlayStation 2 and Xbox make games a mainstream entertainment.

checkpoints.name: Games for everyone
checkpoints.note: Wii Sports, Angry Birds, Candy Crush Saga and Pokemon Go bring games to families and phones, Minecraft lets players build their own worlds, Fortnite becomes a global meeting place, and the Nintendo Switch goes from home to pocket.
